name: Web Application
summary: Tools for authorized testing of web applications and their transport security
description: Scanners, fuzzers, proxies and TLS auditors for assessing web applications you own or are contracted to test. Includes content discovery, parameter mining, a SQL-injection tester, HTTP clients and transport-security checks. Several well-known web scanners (Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP, Nikto, Nuclei) are proprietary or not in Debian and are listed separately with official install links.

external.name: Burp Suite
external.summary: Intercepting proxy and web vulnerability scanner
external.license: Proprietary (PortSwigger). A free Community Edition exists with reduced features.

why.text: Burp Suite is closed-source commercial software and cannot be redistributed by SHADOW; PortSwigger provides the installer directly.

how.text: Download the Community or Professional edition installer for Linux from PortSwigger and run it; Professional requires a licence.

external.name: OWASP ZAP
external.summary: Open-source web application scanner and intercepting proxy
external.license: Apache-2.0 (open source), but no current package in Debian.

why.text: ZAP is free and open source but is not currently packaged in Debian; the project ships cross-platform installers and a container image.

how.text: Install from the official Linux installer or run the maintained Docker image as described in the ZAP documentation.

external.name: Nikto
external.summary: Web server scanner for known issues and dangerous files
external.license: GPL-2.0 for the program; Debian files the package under non-free because of the terms of its bundled databases.

why.text: Debian trixie carries Nikto only in the non-free component. Shadow OS uses Debian main only, so no package is offered; upstream recommends running it from a git checkout.

how.text: Clone the official repository and run program/nikto.pl; it needs only Perl, which is already installed.

external.name: Nuclei
external.license: MIT (open source), not packaged in Debian.

why.text: Nuclei and its templates are released on a rapid cadence outside Debian; ProjectDiscovery publishes binaries and an installer.

how.text: Download the release binary for your architecture from the Nuclei releases page, or install with Go; then run nuclei -update-templates.
